text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a development practice where code changes are regularly merged into a shared repository. The heart of this system is the CI pipeline, which automatically builds the software and runs a suite of tests every time a developer submits new code. This means computers handle the repetitive work, checking for compile errors, broken features, or performance problems. Instead of discovering these issues days later, teams catch problems early, often within minutes of the change. Because the pipeline alerts developers immediately, fixing a small bug is faster and cheaper than waiting for a major failure. Ultimately, CI improves software quality and keeps the whole team confident and productive.
